messages:
Olivia M: Hi team — dentist scheduled an extraction tomorrow but claim was denied as "not eligible". I enrolled during open enrollment and my card shows Redwood plan, but the provider says member status = inactive. Appointment is 8:30am. Help?

Ravi (People Ops): Sorry that happened. Two quick things: do you have your member ID and the EOB/denial message? Sometimes carrier shows inactive if payroll enrollment and carrier sync haven't finished, or if prior COBRA/previous employer record overlaps.

Olivia M: Member ID: D321009876. EOB says "coverage terminated 2026-06-30" even though my effective date is 2026-07-01 per my enrollment confirmation. I don't have COBRA. I uploaded the carrier screenshot to this thread.

June - Benefits: Thanks Olivia. Typical flow: we can issue a same-day employer letter confirming active coverage effective 2026-07-01 and escalate to the carrier for an override/retroactive fix. To expedite we need: enrollment confirmation screenshot (you said you have it) + last payroll stub showing deductions or confirmation that benefits deduction started. If you already sent docs to benefits@redwood.com, reply here.

Olivia M: I have the enrollment confirmation email and a payroll screenshot showing deduction on 2026-07-01. Sent both to benefits just now with subject EXACT: "URGENT: ELIGIBILITY OVERRIDE - Olivia M - DENTAL"

BenefitsBot: ✅ Ticket created: #BEN-5122 — "Eligibility override / denial for dental extraction". Assigned to June. Expected carrier escalation window: same day for provider overrides; retroactive member record fixes may take 3-5 business days. Reply with attachments or confirm if you need the company letter.

June - Benefits: I see the ticket and docs. We'll generate a signed temporary coverage letter for the clinic you can present at check-in; we'll also call provider relations and request the carrier to process a provider-side acceptance pending member-record correction. If the provider requires a pre-auth number, ask them to accept the letter and give us their billing contact so we can push the pre-auth.

Billing - SmileDent: We can proceed if we receive a formal proof of active coverage listing member ID and effective date. Email billing@smiledent.com and attach the employer letter; include patient DOB and appointment reference so we can attach the doc to the claim.

Ravi (People Ops): June — can you please include a line that the employer letter should not include SSN and should state we requested carrier override due to apparent sync delay? Also note the claim ID if they re-submit.

June - Benefits: Will do. Sample employer letter text we'll use:

"To whom it may concern,
This letter confirms that Olivia Meyer (DOB 1992-11-02), member ID D321009876, is an active enrollee in Redwood Inference dental plan with coverage effective 2026-07-01. This document is provided as temporary proof of coverage while we resolve an administrative eligibility discrepancy with the carrier.
Sincerely,
Redwood Benefits Team"

Olivia M: Thank you! Rough timeline? I'm worried they'll charge me up front if they can't verify.

June - Benefits: We will email the signed PDF within 30-60 minutes. If the clinic insists on payment, ask them to bill as "pending insurance" and take the employer letter — we will follow up with a claim appeal/adjustment once carrier corrects the member record. We'll also request a expedited claims review and ask for a reversal of any patient balance if denial was in error.

BenefitsBot: Ticket BEN-5122 updated: employer letter uploaded and provider relations contacted. Please confirm if clinic received the PDF or if you need us to resend to billing@smiledent.com.

Olivia M: Got the PDF and forwarded to SmileDent billing. They said they'll use it to proceed and kept my appointment slot. Deep breath — thanks everyone!! :relieved:
